h1: Winning UGC Videos for Your Facebook Ads
lead: Make scroll-stopping Facebook UGC ads that show your product in use and give shoppers a reason to click, without booking a creator.
card: A Facebook video of the pale-blue bottle, as a square or a tall clip.

faq.q: What is an AI Facebook UGC ad?
faq.a: It is a Facebook clip that looks like someone showing your product. An AI actor and a voice do the demo. You did not book a creator or a studio.

faq.q: Does this kind of ad work on Facebook?
faq.a: Yes. A clip of the product in use sits in the feed more naturally than a glossy brand film. You can make one opening for each buyer you sell to.

faq.q: Can I stop paying a creator for every Facebook test?
faq.a: Yes. Each test comes out of your plan. You are not waiting on a new invoice before the next opening.

faq.q: Do these videos follow Facebook's ad rules?
faq.a: Yes, when the offer is true and the product is the one you ship. Do not invent a buyer, and do not claim a result you have not seen. We do not submit the ad for you.

faq.q: Will people know the ad is made by AI?
faq.a: The clip is built to feel like a creator video in the feed. Say it is AI when Facebook asks you to. Do not treat hiding that as the goal.

faq.q: How fast can I get a Facebook ad file?
faq.a: You can have a file in minutes. Pick an actor, set the first line, and you are not holding the launch for a camera crew.

faq.q: What does a Facebook video cost in credits?
faq.a: Yes. A video spends 24, 40, 60, or 120 credits for 6, 10, 15, or 30 seconds. A photo spends 24. Starter is $24.50 a month for 200 credits, Pro is $35 for 300, and Premium is $63 for 600. You see the cost before you start. A failed job returns those credits.

faq.q: Where should the price and the offer line go?
faq.a: Put the price and the offer where the player buttons will not cover them. You add that text in the editor after download.
